title: Revealing the Nonlinear Amplification of Radiation Reaction Effects via Vortex Radiation
abstract: Radiation reaction (RR), the back-action of emitted radiation on an accelerated charge, dominates the dynamics of ultrarelativistic electrons in an intense electromagnetic field. We derive an analytical formula for the RR-inclusive harmonic spectrum of vortex $γ$-ray emission in monochromatic-wave nonlinear inverse Thomson scattering (NITS), extend it to finite pulses under the slowly varying envelope approximation (SVEA), and take the Landau-Lifshitz (LL) solution as the starting point. We find that once cumulative RR on the oscillation radius over hundreds of cycles becomes non-negligible, the laser intensity nonlinearly amplifies RR through the modified longitudinal drift velocity, reshaping the vortex emission. For monochromatic approximation of long pulse flat-top laser, harmonic band acquire MeV-scale red shifts and spectral compression, producing overlap; higher harmonics show anomalous polarization transitions, so the superposed ellipticity departs from the RR-free case. For a $\sin^2$ envelope, the lower edge red-shifts while the upper cutoff stays fixed, broadening the band, and individual polarization transitions remain analogous to RR-free case. These harmonic-resolved spectral and polarization fingerprints constitute a self-referenced multidimensional diagnostic of RR effects that complements energy-spectrum measurements and, through the RR-inclusive scaling law between the polarization and laser amplitude, provide an independent route to measuring the laser intensity. These results have direct implications for bright high-energy $γ$-ray sources and the modeling of extreme astrophysical environments such as neutron-star magnetospheres.
